Subject: Runtime stability concerns ahead of SDK cutover

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We ran the sandbox load tests overnight and saw token spikes on a subset of calls (mostly long chat sessions + document embeds) that triggered 429s from our side and some timeouts on your hosted endpoint /v1/generate. We need a short, practical plan for the cutover: recommended retry/backoff values, timeout defaults, and the minimal SDK change set to flip endpoints without user-visible regressions.

Can your team send a concise checklist we can hand to our engineering ops to schedule the change next week? Also shout if you want us to join a short runbook review.

Thanks —
Samira
Head of Integrations, VelociPay
——

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Runtime stability concerns ahead of SDK cutover

Samira —

Appreciate the signal and the test artifacts. I put together a short operational checklist and attached a one-page Cutover Plan (velocipay-cutover-plan-20260919.pdf) plus a small ZIP with SDK samples for retries/timeouts. High-level ask: aim for a staged cutover (canary -> 25% -> 100%) over one business day with a rollback hang at each stage.

Key checklist (summary):
- Pre-cutover: finalize test vectors + golden prompts; confirm max seq length and typical embed batch sizes.
- Config changes: update client endpoint to the new route, enable header-based routing (x-rw-env: canary) for 24 hrs.
- Retries: implement idempotent-safe retry with exponential backoff and jitter; prefer 3 max attempts for 429s, 2 for 503s.
- Timeouts: client-side per-request timeout = 20s for generation calls, 60s for long streaming sessions (with sub-heartbeat).
- Rate limiting: honor x-rw-rate-limit headers; implement local token bucket to smooth bursts.
- Observability: forward debug headers (x-rw-request-id) back to us on failure; keep verbose logs for the first 2 hours post-cutover.
- Rollback: immediate DNS/route flip to previous endpoint if error rate > 5% sustained for 3 minutes.

Camila attached two code samples in the ZIP: one Node.js snippet showing a retry decorator and one Python example that wraps streaming with a reconnect pattern. Aditya added a short note on smart routing and KV-cache warmup (below).

I've proposed a 30-minute runbook review on Monday; please suggest a time. I'll be on the call along with Camila and Aditya.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime stability concerns ahead of SDK cutover

Adding infra notes — a few operational knobs that helped other customers:

- Smart routing: route heavy generation traffic to Dedicated pools where possible. If using hosted, enable model-variant fallback (gptx-13b -> gptx-6b) for non-critical long-running sessions.
- KV cache warmup: pre-warm KV cache with the top 500 frequent prefixes during canary to avoid cold-cache latency spikes.
- Batching window: for high-throughput embeddings, use a 50-150ms batching window; it reduces per-token cost and smooths spikes.
- Observability hooks: add a short script to post prometheus-style metrics (latency, downstream 429 rate) to our shared Drive link every minute during the cutover window so we can monitor together.

Operational thresholds we recommend toggling in the first 2 hours:
- Error budget threshold: pause cutover if 5xx rate > 1% over a 5-min sliding window.
- Latency threshold: pause if p95 generation latency increases > 2x baseline for 10+ minutes.

I'll join the runbook review and stay on-call during the canary.

—Aditya
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
